scope: Published measurements related to tracer release after an exterior wash and redistribution into a finite receiver. Both comparisons are descriptive.

experiments.citation: Boyer and Zasadzinski (2007), ACS Nano, Figure 2 and accompanying text on page 179
experiments.system: Single-bilayer DPPC vesicles loaded with carboxyfluorescein, buffer-only control after removal of external dye by chromatography.
experiments.readout: Suspension fluorescence dequenching. A lysed-sample measurement supplies the total-dye reference.
experiments.limits: The reported half-time is a lower bound. Absolute retained molecule counts, trapped aqueous volume and separate exterior concentrations are unavailable for this comparison.

experiments.citation: Bachler et al. (2021), Analytical Chemistry, Figures 2A-B and 5B-C and label-free permeation analysis
experiments.system: Rhodamine 6G in one aqueous droplet, initially dye-free buffer in the other, across a symmetric DOPC bilayer.
experiments.readout: Each fluorescence image was normalized to its total signal. At sampling, the investigators separated donor and receiver droplets and measured each side's LC-MS peak area.
experiments.limits: Both permeability estimates use the observations in the paper. Later sampling may have cooled the droplets. The planar interface and the charge of rhodamine 6G limit comparison with a neutral vesicle tracer. The experiment used no wash.
